question.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3})=1
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a\pi +\pi n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $[-1,0).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =0+2\pi n.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+2\pi n \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+\pi n.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=-\frac{1}{6}.$
